cards.b: Checks each item in turn from the start until the target is found or the list ends. Works on unsorted lists.
On a sorted list, compare with the middle item and discard the half that cannot contain the target; repeat.
mid = (low + high) DIV 2, rounding down. For indices 0 to 7 the middle is 3.

cards.f: Binary search: the target is bigger than the middle item
cards.b: Search the upper half: set low = mid + 1.

cards.f: Binary search: when does it stop with 'not found'?
cards.b: When low becomes greater than high.
Compares neighbouring items and swaps them if out of order; repeats passes until a pass has no swaps.
The largest unsorted item has moved to the end of the list.

cards.f: Why does a swap need a temporary variable?
cards.b: Copying one value over another would lose the overwritten value, so it is held in a temp first.

cards.f: Why use a swapped flag in bubble sort?
cards.b: To stop as soon as a whole pass makes no swaps, avoiding unnecessary passes.
Keep splitting the list in half until every sub-list has one item.
Compare the first items of two sorted lists, take the smaller, repeat; this builds a bigger sorted list.
Works on unsorted data and is very simple to write.
Much faster on long lists because the search area is halved each time.
Bubble sort: simple, no extra memory, slow on long lists. Merge sort: much faster on long lists but needs more memory.
The target is last or not in the list, so every item is checked.

short.q: Explain why binary search cannot be used on the unsorted list 9 2 14 6.
short.model: Binary search compares with the middle item and discards half the list. In an unsorted list the target could be in the discarded half, so it might be missed.
points: works by discarding half based on the middle item
needs sorted data, otherwise target could be in the discarded half

short.q: Show the list 6 2 9 4 after each pass of a bubble sort (ascending).
short.model: Pass 1: 2 6 4 9. Pass 2: 2 4 6 9. Pass 3: no swaps, so it is sorted: 2 4 6 9.
points: pass 2: 2 4 6 9 and final pass with no swaps

short.q: A sorted list is 3 8 12 15 21 27 34 40. Trace a binary search for 12 and give the items checked.
short.model: Items checked: 15 (mid index 3), then 8 (mid index 1), then 12 (mid index 2) where it is found.

short.q: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of merge sort compared with bubble sort.
short.model: Advantage: much faster on long lists. Disadvantage: needs extra memory and is more complex to code.

short.q: A list of 50,000 sorted customer numbers is searched many times a day. Which search should be used and why?
short.model: Binary search, because the list is already sorted and halving the search area each time is far quicker than checking numbers one by one.
points: sorted data/halves each time so much faster
